title: Weak Verbs — Class I
subtitle: Dēman, hīeran — the dental suffix.
objectives: Read and translate authentic Old English poetry and prose.

sections.heading: Content
sections.body: Weak verbs form their past tense by adding a dental suffix (-d- or -t-), not by ablaut. Class I weak verbs have -e- in the infinitive and present tense. Present: ic dēme, þū dēmest, hē dēmeþ. Past: ic dēmde, þū dēmdest, hē dēmde. Past participle: gedēmed.
